headline_marked: HC petition seeks [[Bar Council election in 30 days]], challenges ad-hoc committee
headline: HC petition seeks Bar Council election in 30 days, challenges ad-hoc committee
summary: A writ petition has been filed in the High Court seeking the suspension of the current ad-hoc committee and a fresh election for the Bangladesh Bar Council within a month.
details: A writ petition has been filed in the High Court challenging the legality of the ad-hoc committee currently running the Bangladesh Bar Council.
The petition, filed by Supreme Court lawyer Yunus Ali Akhand on Wednesday, seeks an order directing authorities to hold a Bar Council election within the next 30 days.
The plea also asks the court to suspend the current committee's activities until the election is completed, naming the law secretary and other authorities as respondents.
The Bar Council has seen significant changes since the fall of the the Sheikh Hasina government on August 5, 2024, including the appointment of new leadership.
A 14-member ad-hoc committee was initially formed by the law ministry on May 28, 2025, to prepare for a fresh election, but the scheduled May 19 election was postponed indefinitely.
Following the suspension, the government formed a new 15-member ad-hoc committee on Tuesday, with Attorney General Ruhul Quddus as chairman.
The new committee's tenure is set to run for one year from July 1, while critics like the National Lawyers Alliance have argued that the Bar Council law has no clear provision for such a body.
caption:
Can the Bangladesh Bar Council be run by an ad-hoc committee? A High Court petition now challenges its legality.

A writ petition has been filed in the High Court challenging the legality of the ad-hoc committee currently running the Bangladesh Bar Council.

The petition, filed by Supreme Court lawyer Yunus Ali Akhand on Wednesday, seeks an order directing authorities to hold a Bar Council election within the next 30 days.

The plea also asks the court to suspend the current committee's activities until the election is completed, naming the law secretary and other authorities as respondents.

The Bar Council has seen significant changes since the fall of the the Sheikh Hasina government on August 5, 2024, including the appointment of new leadership.

A 14-member ad-hoc committee was initially formed by the law ministry on May 28, 2025, to prepare for a fresh election, but the scheduled May 19 election was postponed indefinitely.

Following the suspension, the government formed a new 15-member ad-hoc committee on Tuesday, with Attorney General Ruhul Quddus as chairman.

The new committee's tenure is set to run for one year from July 1, while critics like the National Lawyers Alliance have argued that the Bar Council law has no clear provision for such a body.

headline_marked: 2 [[Two die in fishing trawler fire]] in Karnaphuli River
headline: 2 Two die in fishing trawler fire in Karnaphuli River
summary: Two crew members of the FB Desh fishing trawler died from burns on their way to Dhaka for treatment after a generator spark spark caused a fire in the engine room.
details: Two crew members of the fishing trawler FB Desh died on Tuesday night while being transported to Dhaka for advanced treatment after a fire broke out on the vessel.
The victims, greasers Rubel and Shah Alam, succumbed to their injuries on the way to the capital. Their bodies were subsequently handed over to their families in Patuakhali and Noakhali for burial.
The fire started around 12:45 pm on Tuesday in the engine room of the trawler, which was anchored in the Sadarghat section of the Karnaphuli River in Chattogram.

Six people were burnt in the total incident. Three victims—winch operator Nizam Uddin, diver Russell, and sailor Siddique Ahmed—were treated at Chattogram Medical College Hospital and have since been discharged.
A cadet engineer, Ashiquzzaman Tamim, remains in the ICU of the National Burn and Plastic Surgery Institute in Dhaka in critical condition.
The vessel had anchored near the Sadarghat Sampan Dock on Monday afternoon after returning from a sea fishing trip.
Trawler officials believe the fire was caused by a spark in the generator. A general diary has been filed at the city's Sadarghat Police Station regarding the incident.
caption:
A generator spark in a fishing trawler's engine room left two crew members dead and several others injured.

Two crew members of the fishing trawler FB Desh died on Tuesday night while being transported to Dhaka for advanced treatment after a fire broke out on the vessel.

The victims, greasers Rubel and Shah Alam, succumbed to their injuries on the way to the capital. Their bodies were subsequently handed over to their families in Patuakhali and Noakhali for burial.

The fire started around 12:45 pm on Tuesday in the engine room of the trawler, which was anchored in the Sadarghat section of the Karnaphuli River in Chattogram.

Six people were burnt in the total incident. Three victims—winch operator Nizam Uddin, diver Russell, and sailor Siddique Ahmed—were treated at Chattogram Medical College Hospital and have since been discharged.

A cadet engineer, Ashiquzzaman Tamim, remains in the ICU of the National Burn and Plastic Surgery Institute in Dhaka in critical condition.

The vessel had anchored near the Sadarghat Sampan Dock on Monday afternoon after returning from a sea fishing trip.

Trawler officials believe the fire was caused by a spark in the generator. A general diary has been filed at the city's Sadarghat Police Station regarding the incident.
